big_idea: A CALENDAR shows DAYS, WEEKS, MONTHS, HOLIDAYS, and SEASONS.
learning_intention: We are learning to read a calendar.
student_learning_goal: I can read the date and find days, weeks, months on a calendar.
success_criteria: I can find DAYS, WEEKS, and MONTHS.
I can name a HOLIDAY and a SEASON.
lesson_specific_materials: OPTIONAL: Roo and Cal — if available; otherwise teacher voices both characters in two distinct voices, or substitutes two stuffed animals / paper-bag puppets / pictures on the anchor poster. Activity is unaffected.

minds_on.hook: Cal: TODAY is the 4th of May! May is a MONTH. There are 7 DAYS in a WEEK. Let's find some HOLIDAYS!
minds_on.teacher_script:
Bring children to the carpet. Roo and Cal puppets. 'Friends — yesterday mass and capacity. Today CALENDAR.'

Introduce vocabulary. Write CALENDAR, SEASON on chart. 'Calendar = a grid that shows days, weeks, months. Season = part of the year.'

Demonstrate. Show a wall calendar of the current month. 'Today is ___ (point to the date). The MONTH is ___ (point to the top).'

Point to Sunday-Saturday header. '7 DAYS in a WEEK. Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday.'

Point to a holiday. 'This day has a star — that's a HOLIDAY. Like Canada Day on July 1st, or Family Day in February.'

Point to seasons. 'Now is SPRING (or whichever). Then SUMMER, FALL, WINTER. 4 SEASONS.'

More examples:
- How many days in this month? (Count.)
- What day is the 15th?
- Which Canadian holiday is in October? (Thanksgiving.)

'Cal says — calendars help us PLAN.'

'Today we read calendars and find dates.'

steps.instruction: Whole group: find today, this week, this month. Identify a holiday and the season.
steps.teacher_prompt: Say: 'Find today. What day is it?'

steps.instruction: Three stations. Station A: Find the Date — pair finds 5 specific dates. Station B: Count Days — pair counts days in the month. Station C: Holidays — pair finds 4 Canadian holidays on a calendar.
Stretch challenge at Station C: name the SEASON for each holiday.
Discuss the calendar grid. 'Rows = weeks. Columns = days. Each cell = one day.'
steps.teacher_prompt: Demonstrate by tracing rows and columns.
Stop at each pair. Ask 'What's the date?' Mark the tracker.

differentiation.for_emerging: Stay at Station A. Find today's date only.
differentiation.for_extending: Stretch at Station C: name season for each holiday.
differentiation.for_ell_or_iep: Provide a sentence frame: 'Today is ___. The month is ___.'
differentiation.for_movement_learners: Children walk to a wall calendar and physically point to dates.

formative_check.what_to_look_for: Three signals: reads the date; finds days/weeks/months; names a holiday or season.

discussion_prompts: How many days in a week?
Name a Canadian holiday and its season.
consolidation.exit_routine: Each child writes today's date: 'Today is ___ (day) ___ (date) ___ (month).'

assessment_in_this_lesson.rationale: Lesson 4 captures E2.3 mastery for calendar reading.

expanded_walkthrough.title: When the child can name today but not COUNT FORWARD a week — repairing the static-date trap at Grade 1
expanded_walkthrough.rationale:
The most common Grade-1 trap on E2.3 is the static-date trap: the child can read today's date (e.g., 'Monday May 4'), but cannot count forward to find next Monday or the day in 5 days. They miss that calendars are NAVIGABLE.

This matters because calendar use is for planning, which requires forward and backward counting.

The walkthrough covers when a child can't navigate.
expanded_walkthrough.setup: Pair is at Station A. Asked 'what day is in 5 days?' from today (Monday May 4). Child says 'I don't know'.
expanded_walkthrough.teacher_script:
Crouch. 'You know today is Monday. Cal says — count FORWARD on the calendar.'

Guide. Touch today's date. 'Monday — 1. Tuesday — 2. Wednesday — 3. Thursday — 4. Friday — 5. So 5 days from today is Friday.'

Generalise. 'Cal says — calendars let us COUNT forward AND backward. Touch today, count.'

If still stuck: provide a number-line strip of the next 7 days. 'Use this to count.'

Long-term recovery: every calendar use practices counting forward.
expected_student_responses: (Confused) Reads today but can't count forward
common_misconceptions: Calendar = today only. (Repair: calendar shows past + future.)
Counting forward is hard. (Repair: use finger touch.)
Different months don't connect. (Repair: months follow each other.)

worksheet_brief.purpose: Independent practice of E2.3 calendar reading.

parts_outline.task: Look at the calendar. Find today's date. Find next Friday. Mark them.
Count days in the month. Write the number.
Name 2 Canadian holidays and their seasons.
